title.narrative: Promoting Socio-Economic Resilience & Social Cohesion in Niassa (JP-UNH-IOM)
Promoting Socio-Economic Resilience & Social Cohesion in Niassa (JP-UNH-IOM)

description.narrative:
The project has an overarching goal of promoting socio-economic resilience and social cohesion in Niassa Province through an integrated development and peace-building approach. The main objective, as set out as the project's objective is "to enhance community resilience and stability through inclusive development and improved living conditions in Niassa Province".
This objective is underpinned by three main outcomes;
1) The resilience of communities, especially women and youth at risk of or affected by conflict, is strengthened through the promotion of social cohesion and conflict resolution mechanisms.
2) The Government presence and capacities at provincial and local levels are increased, strengthening service delivery, governance, accountability and citizen participation.
3) Communities, especially women and youth at risk of or affected by conflict, are empowered through economic inclusion and livelihood opportunities and the promotion of improved living conditions and stability.
Four districts in the south western parts of Niassa have been chosen for the intervention; Marrupa, Metarica, Maua, Nipepe.
The number of direct expected beneficiaries are: - 236 457 individuals (women and man, youth and children) form vulnerable communities of the 4 target districts (77.808 in Marrupa, 68.260 in Maua, 45.303 in Metarica and 45.086 in Nipepe). - 20,000 people with access to birth certificates and ID cards (of which 12,000 women and 8,000 men, comprised of 10,000 youth). - 6000 people (with at least 50% women) with increased security of tenure at settlement level - 300 participants supported in capacity development on planning for resilience and engaged in participatory planning processes. - 200 participants trained and capacitated in building activities on resilient construction. - 600 people, between men and women, directly benefiting from income generation packages. - 160 members of peace clubs trained in eight communities (20 in each).

The United Nations Human Settlement Programme (UN Habitat) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) have submitted a three-year joint project document entitled "Nexus Niassa: Promoting socio-economic resilience and social cohesion in Niassa province through an integrated approach to development and peacebuilding".
Purpose and target group
The aim is to increase the resilience and stability of communities through inclusive development and improved living conditions in Niassa. To achieve the overall purpose, the project will focus on three result areas;
Strengthening the resilience of four identified communities, through conflict management and work to strengthen community cohesion and build positive social relations, with a particular focus on women and young people who are at risk or directly affected by the conflict in the neighbouring province of Cabo Delgado. Strengthening the state's presence at district and provincial level, through strengthening community services, administration, accountability, and civil society participation.
Empowering communities, especially women and children at risk or directly affected by through capacity development in financial inclusion and livelihoods, as well as improved living conditions and stability.
The project will apply an integrated and flexible approach and work with local authorities, communities and individuals, where UNHabitat will support state institutions with territorial planning and development, and IOM will work community empowering and stabilizing and implement interventions tailored to each community where the project is active. The project has a total budget of SEK 78 million.
The target group for the project is decision-makers and staff in public administration at all levels, districts, provinces and indirectly also state, local leaders and administrative associations in the communities where the project operates, civil society organizations, as well as residents of the identified communities with a focus (though not exclusively) on women and young people (both young women and men) as well as internally displaced people.
The project counts that direct beneficiaries will be: - 236 457 inhabitants of the 4 target districts (77.808 in Marrupa, 68.260 in Maua, 45.303 in Metarica and 45.086 in Nipepe) with improved access to participatory governance and service provision (with priority on education and health). - 20,000 people with access to birth certificates and ID cards (of which 12,000 women and 8,000 men, comprised of 10,000 youth). - 6000 people (with at least 50% women) with increased security of tenure at settlement level 300 participants supported in capacity development on planning for resilience and engaged in participatory planning processes. - 200 participants trained and capacitated in building activities on resilient construction. - 600 people, between men and women, directly benefitting from income generation packages. 160 members of peace clubs trained in eight communities (20 in each).

United Nations Human Settlement Programme (UN Habitat) och International Organization for Migration (IOM) har inkommit med ett treårigt gemensamt projektdokument med titeln "Nexus Niassa: Främja socioekonomisk motståndskraft och social sammanhållning i Niassaprovinsen genom en integrerad strategi för utveckling och fredsbyggande”.
Syfte och målgrupp
Syftet är att öka samhällens motståndskraft och stabilitet genom inkluderande utveckling och förbättrade levnadsvillkor i Niassa. För att uppnå det övergripande syftet kommer projektet att fokusera på tre resultatområden;
Stärkande av fyra identifierade samhällens resiliens, genom konflikthantering och arbete för att stärka samhörighet i samhällena samt bygga positiva sociala relationer med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar som är i riskzon eller direkt påverkade av konflikten i grannprovinsen Cabo Delgado. Stärkande av statens närvaro på distrikts och provinsnivå, genom stärkande av samhällstjänster, förvaltning, ansvarsutkrävande, och deltagande från civilsamhället.
Stärka samhällen, speciellt kvinnor och barn i riskzon eller direkt påverkade av konflikten, genom kapacitetsutveckling inom finansiell inkludering och försörjningsmöjligheter samt förbättrade levnadsvillkor och stabilitet.
Projektet kommer att tillämpa ett integrerat och flexibelt tillvägagångssätt och arbeta med lokala myndigheter, samhällen och individer, där UNHabitat kommer att stödja statliga institutioner med territoriell planering och utveckling, och IOM kommer att arbeta samhällsstärkande och stabiliserande och genomföra insatser som är skräddarsydda för varje samhälle där projektet är aktivt. Projektet har en total budget på 78 MSEK.
Målgruppen för projektet är beslutsfattare och personal inom offentlig förvaltning på alla nivåer, distrikt provins och indirekt även statlig, lokala ledare och administrativa föreningar i de samhällena där projektet är verksamt, civilsamhällsorganisationer, samt invånare i de identifierade samhällena med ett fokus (dock ej exkluderande) på kvinnor och ungdomar (både unga kvinnor och män) samt internflyktingar.
Projektet beräknar att nå: -236 457 individer i de fyra distrikt som projektet är Verksamt 77 808 i Marrupa, 68 260 i Maua, 45 303 i Metarica och 45 086 i Nipepe och förbättra deras delaktighet i offentlig förvaltning och tillgång till samhällstjänster (med fokus på hälsa och utbildning). -Vidare beräknas 20 000 männsikor få tillgång till födelsebevis och ID kort, 6000 individer varav minst 50% kvinnor med stärkta markrättigheter för bosättning, 300 personer stöds med kapacitetsutveckling för samhällsplanering med fokus på resiliens, 200 personer kommer tränas inom resilient byggande, 600 personer kommer ta del av inkomstgenererande aktiviteter och 160 medlemmar i fredsklubbarna från åtta samhällen kommer att ta del av kapacitetsutveckling inom fredsbyggande.

description.narrative:
Given that the programme is just coming out of the inception phase, tangible results are few. Many preparatory actions have been made however. On a general level, following preliminary steps have been carried out:
• UNtoUN MoU between UNHABITAT and IOM finalized (Dec 2024), clarifying roles and budget allocations, and amended in April to facilitate disbursement • Recruitment of Joint Project Implementation Unit (JPIU) advanced: core staff in place (Admin Officer, Finance Assistant, Team Leader, specialists in gender, communication, M&E and environment), with key posts under recruitment (district focal points, GIS & data management officer, resilient construction assistants, logistics and operations coordinator). • IOM management structure was established with senior leadership and the Programme Manager based in Maputo. A dedicated technical supervision team operates from Pemba, comprising a Programme Officer, Project Assistants, administrative personnel and monitoring and Evaluation support. • Programme visibility enhanced through the production of the Nexus Fact Sheet (Aug 2025).
Progress have also been on almost all the outputs:
OUTPUT 1.1 • From 4 to 11 May 2025 Mapping mission conducted to Marrupa, Maua, Nipepe and Metarica. Conducted scoping missions to Maua and Marrupa. OUTPUT 1.2 • Launch of preparatory steps for the Niassa spatial analysis through Matrix of Functions (MoF) , to start October 2025, with training of district focal points on spatial and infrastructure data collection and analysis. • Alignment of methodology with earlier Spatial Analysis of Northern Mozambique (2023), whose findings are already guiding programme implementation. OUTPUT 1.3 • Posting of Call for Expression of Interest (CEI) in September 2025 for Implementing Partners (IPs) to facilitate and lead locally driven and culturally appropriate community dialogues for peace, and to establish, train, and support locally owned community peace committees. OUTPUT 1.4 • Supported the 4th Youth Observatory in Niassa, engaging 300 youth in dialogue on sustainable development and public policy, reinforcing the Nexus projects commitment to inclusive, communitydriven peacebuilding.
OUTPUT 2.1 • Joint UNHabitat/IOM mission (37 August 2025) in the four districts introduced the programme, mobilized district administrations, and designated focal points. • Baseline data collected: institutional self assessments, preliminary questionnaires, rapid participatory mapping, and critical infrastructures rapid assessments. • Priority neighborhoods and communities preidentified using socioeconomic and climate vulnerability criteria: Metarica Neighborhood, Maua Neighborhood, Nipepe, Vila Sede, Morrico Marrupa, Cafezeiro, Nungo. • Territorial development opportunity identified: Lalaua Nipepe road corridor (DH Mining), transforming the development triangle into a trapezium recognition of the collapsed Niorenge bridge (Morrico) as a catalytic intervention to boost the district's rapid development. OUTPUT 2.2 • Publication of Call for Expression of Interest (CEI) planned for September to identify an Implementing Partner (IP) to mentor district level civil society organizations (CSOs) receiving small grants for community based peacebuilding initiatives OUTPUT 2.3 • Drafted and launched the Unit Price Framework Agreement (UPFA) for infrastructure rehabilitation across four district based lots. • Compiled a preliminary list of infrastructures with high probability for intervention (schools, health centers, administrative buildings, water systems, bridge in Morrico). • Defined UPFA as the mechanism to preselect firms at unit rates, ensuring procurement readiness before RFA finalization. OUTPUT 2.4 • Held joint strategic preliminary meetings at provincial level with Provincial Service for Justice (SPJT) and Provincial Service for Civil Identification (SPIC) in preparation for the rollout of legal identity activities.
OUTPUT 3.1 • Target neighborhoods and communities preidentified: Metarica (Bairro 2), Maua (Bairro 4), Nipepe (Vila Sede and Morrico) and Marrupa (Cafezeiro and Nungo). • Preparation of Call for Proposals (CFP) to be launched in November 2025 for CSOs/NGOs to lead community mobilization, housing pilots, and public space implementation. • Strategy developed to combine NGO mobilization with a specialized company for DUAT facilitation, including provision for community DUATs where appropriate. • Agreement that physical works (street opening, drainage) will be executed by UPFA contractors (Output 2.3), ensuring integration. • Housing approach defined: 20 resilient houses built as model units, distributed across districts, using on the job training and mutirão community mobilization, with beneficiaries selected through vulnerability assessments. • Public spaces are confirmed as part of the neighborhood upgrading package to ensure an urbanist vision, including areas for leisure and community interaction. OUTPUT 3.2 • Community Based Planning (CBP) training for 33 government officials held in Lichinga (1115 August 2025) promoting locally led planning and a shift toward community centered approaches to strengthen ownership and sustainability of infrastructure initiatives OUTPUT 3.3 • Posted a Call for Expression of Interest (CEI) in May 2025 for Implementing Partners (IPs) to develop locally driven and culturally appropriate income generation opportunities.
